open_obligations: Note that ICM uses no weak labels, so the setting differs from Burns et al.'s.
Check whether a weak supervisor could elicit the sun concept where ICM cannot.
Note salience is inferred from failure rather than measured.
out.other_title: Open questions on understanding weak-to-strong generalization and salience
out.rationale: Burns et al. ask what makes a concept easy or hard to elicit and how to define salience. Wen et al. report ICM performs at chance on a 'poems mentioning sun are better' task with Llama 70B and attribute this to the concept not being salient; ICM is unsupervised elicitation, not weak-to-strong finetuning, and salience is not formally defined.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: what makes a concept hard to elicit without strong supervision, tested with a deliberately non-salient preference

text: The paper reports a task designed to be impossible for unsupervised elicitation: comparison pairs where poems mentioning 'sun' are preferred while the model is only told to judge which poem is better. With Llama 70B, ICM performs no better than random guessing, which the authors attribute to the concept not being salient to the pretrained model.
title: Unsupervised elicitation fails when the target concept is not salient (sun-poem task)
